title: BCCI Names India ODI, T20I Squads for West Indies; Rohit Retains Place
excerpt: Shubman Gill will captain a 15-man ODI squad for the three-match home series starting September 27, with Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli retained, Dhruv Jurel preferred over Rishabh Pant as the second wicketkeeper, and Shreyas Iyer set to lead the T20I side.
body:
• The BCCI on September 16 named India's ODI and T20I squads for the home white-ball series against the West Indies: three ODIs starting September 27, five T20Is from October 6.
  • Shubman Gill will captain the ODI side with KL Rahul as vice-captain; Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli retain their places as the 2027 World Cup buildup continues.
  • Dhruv Jurel edged Rishabh Pant for the second wicketkeeper's slot in the ODIs; Pant will instead captain Rest of India in the Irani Cup from October 1.
  • Naman Dhir and Auqib Nabi earned maiden ODI call-ups, Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammed Siraj return, Hardik Pandya misses out through injury, and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made the T20I squad.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India on Tuesday ended weeks of speculation by naming India's squads for the home white-ball series against the West Indies, handing Shubman Gill the ODI captaincy, keeping faith with veterans Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, and rewarding domestic form with two maiden ODI call-ups.

Gill to lead, Rohit and Kohli stay

Gill will lead a 15-man ODI squad with KL Rahul named vice-captain, replacing Shreyas Iyer, who had held the role during the recent ODI assignment against England. The headline news for fans was the retention of Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli, whose places in the 50-over setup have been the subject of persistent debate as India builds toward the 2027 World Cup.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4uoig0gOCVc

The squad features a blend of experience and emerging talent. Alongside Gill, Rohit and Kohli, the batting group includes Ruturaj Gaikwad, Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal — returning to the ODI setup as a backup opener — and new call-up Naman Dhir. The bowling attack comprises Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Kuldeep Yadav and debutant Auqib Nabi, with Ravindra Jadeja retained.

Jadeja and Siraj both return after missing the England tour, a vote of confidence in two senior campaigners. Siraj had initially been part of the ODI plans for England before being withdrawn over workload concerns, while Jadeja — still a question mark for 2027, according to analysts — gets another chance to stake his claim.

The Jurel-Pant call

The biggest selection debate came in the wicketkeeping department. With Ishan Kishan committed to the Asian Games in Japan, a vacancy opened for the backup keeper's slot behind first-choice KL Rahul. The selectors chose Dhruv Jurel, who returns to the ODI setup after last featuring on the tour of Australia, ahead of Rishabh Pant.

https://x.com/BCCI/status/2100239440493052226

Pant was not considered for either white-ball squad despite being theoretically next in line. Instead, he will captain Rest of India in the Irani Cup, starting in Srinagar on October 1, with Sarfaraz Khan as his deputy. The message from the selectors appears clear: Pant is being managed as a red-ball priority, with a two-match Test series against New Zealand and the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia on the horizon.

Hardik misses out, Reddy reshuffled

All-rounder Hardik Pandya is a notable absentee from both squads as he continues his recovery from injury. He has been named in the India A white-ball squad for List A matches against Australia A later this month, with his participation subject to fitness.

Nitish Kumar Reddy, originally named in India's Asian Games squad, has been withdrawn from that campaign to join the ODI squad for the West Indies series instead — a last-minute shuffle that underlines how seriously the selectors are taking the home series. Meanwhile, spinner Varun Chakaravarthy has been ruled out of both the Japan T20 and the Asian Games with a side strain, with Vipraj Nigam brought in as his replacement.

Iyer leads the T20Is, a 15-year-old gets the nod

The T20I squad will be captained by Shreyas Iyer with Tilak Varma as his deputy: Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ishan Kishan (wicketkeeper), Sanju Samson (wicketkeeper), Shivam Dube, Kuldeep Yadav, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav and Mayank Yadav.

The standout selection is 15-year-old prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, whose inclusion in a senior India squad marks one of the boldest youth calls in recent memory. Head coach Gautam Gambhir will remain with the senior ODI squad, while VVS Laxman takes charge of the T20I unit.

Schedule and what's next

The ODI series opens in Thiruvananthapuram on September 27, with the second game in Guwahati on September 30 and the finale in New Chandigarh on October 3. The T20I leg then runs from October 6 in Lucknow through Ranchi, Indore, Hyderabad and Bengaluru, concluding on October 17.

The Asian Games, running concurrently in Japan from September 24 to October 3, explains the split squads — India will also play a one-off T20 international against Japan on September 22 before their campaign begins. With the World Cup a year away, these selections are auditions as much as announcements: every spot in the squad is now contested in public.
nri_angle: The squad shapes India's buildup to the 2027 World Cup, a campaign millions of Indian-origin fans will follow across broadcast and streaming, while the inclusion of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi shows how young the talent pipeline runs.
